publicReleaseNotes:
**The install description's declared hash matched an older file: approving Lamp on the platform said it could not be installed yet; fixed.**

- **Get your team into Lamp.** Settings → Operators explains what each role can do before you send the invitation. Communicator is the default so a teammate can publish updates without managing settings or other operators. Pending invitations show the selected role. On a local copy, open the pending link in the same browser to try the role, or put Lamp online with email enabled to invite someone on another computer.
- **Set up your page and see its identity in Lamp.** Choose an accent colour during local installation and search by city for a time zone during first-run setup. Setup keeps a valid saved zone and suggests the browser zone if the saved one is invalid. The saved page name appears in the workspace, browser tab and sign-in card. Add a wide logo and an optional separate square icon during setup or in Settings → Page. Settings → Look explains invalid colour values and keeps the last saved colour until the new value is valid. Maintenance forms show the chosen time zone.
- **See what customers can see after publishing.** The incident record links to the public page and shows the latest customer-facing update once it is public. The next draft has its own editor. Use the Page and Email previews to check the customer's update. The email preview explains how Lamp chose the incident impact and says when local email is off. Set each affected component's impact before publishing. A correction starts from the original wording and links both public updates. Resolving an incident warns when a manual component status will remain in effect and offers a way back to Automatic.
- **Know what this copy can send.** Notification settings show the actual email and text configuration, explain when a local page cannot be opened by customers, and link to setup instructions. The inactive sender field is hidden and technical deployment inputs are under Details.
- **Change maintenance plans without losing the record.** Cancel with an optional customer reason, reinstate the same window, or cancel it again. Previous subscribers receive the applicable cancellation or change notice. An announcement or change in the last 24 hours replaces the reminder. Public and email notices separate impact from affected services. The public page shows the time range in the page’s time zone. The Delivery log names the maintenance window and notice type. Overview shows when overdue work was due and where to start, complete or cancel it.
- **Review what will move from Sorry.** Dry runs and saved jobs list each supplied field, its outcome and the next action in a searchable, downloadable field ledger. Unsupported resources and shortened values are called out. Notice and update templates retain their original wording and source scope privately. Applying a template leaves the draft's status, audience and affected services for review before publication. Move in sends no notifications and preserves edited templates on undo.
- **Manage installation and connections more clearly.** Hosted setup records the exact migration files D1 confirmed, including after a partial apply, so health reports the observed schema separately from uptime. Native removal checks that both workers.dev Workers and their proven resources are gone and can resume if a provider leaves resources behind. The install guide and local sign-in page explain how to make the CLI available in a new terminal. Jira Service Management and Opsgenie settings keep matcher edits separate from saving a replacement key.
- **Keep the public page readable during a storage interruption.** When Lamp serves the last known status, the page and feeds label when it was generated. A retained page also keeps its uploaded logo.

Upgrading from 1.11.22: back up data and your source changes first, update the checkout to `v1.11.23`, run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `rer deploy` with the same environment and input file. The deploy applies `0082_repeated_maintenance_cancellation.sql` and then `0083_sorry_template_metadata.sql` before starting the updated Worker. Keep the backup and exercise a restored copy. Check sign-in, first-run setup, Settings, incident publication, maintenance cancellation and reinstatement, and your intended mail configuration. Review imported Sorry templates before using them. Preserve the original deployment checkout, ownership records and account credentials for `rer signin`. Earlier installations also follow the retained upgrade notes below, including the migration introduced in 1.11.17, the mail-off instructions in 1.11.19 and keeping `INSTALLATION_KEY` with their private secrets. The checkout keeps rer 0.2.121.

PAGE-009.summary: Public screens name the configured time zone, with exact UTC offsets available in Time details.
PAGE-009.was: Public timestamps and notifications use the configured time zone and offset. Under RL-1, the owner’s S4 exception permits a relative generation label while scripting runs. 1. Every public and notification timestamp displays the configured time zone and UTC offset; page timestamps retain their exact ISO instant as machine-readable data. 2. With scripting available, the generation label is relative and refreshes while the page stays open; its tooltip retains the absolute configured-zone time and offset and its machine-readable value retains the instant. 3. Initial HTML and script-disabled readers see the absolute generation time; incident, maintenance, feed and notification timestamps remain absolute.
PAGE-009.now: Public timestamps use the configured time zone, named on the page with exact UTC offsets available in Time details. Feeds and notifications retain absolute timestamps with the configured offset. Under RL-1, the owner’s S4 exception permits a relative generation label while scripting runs. 1. Public page timestamps use the configured zone’s local time and name, with exact UTC offsets in Time details and ISO instants as machine-readable data. Feed and notification timestamps retain the configured UTC offset. 2. With scripting available, the generation label is relative and refreshes while the page stays open. Its tooltip gives the absolute configured-zone time, Time details gives the offset, and its machine-readable value retains the instant. 3. Initial HTML and script-disabled readers see the absolute generation time; incident, maintenance, feed and notification timestamps remain absolute.

MOVE-001.summary: Sorry dry runs and saved jobs count exposed notice and update templates and account for every supplied field path, with reasons and next actions; unknown nested fields, shortened wording and unsupported resource files cannot be silently ignored.
MOVE-001.was: Move in previews a switch from Statuspage, Better Stack, Instatus or Sorry before writing Lamp records, and applies only the exact source and page state the owner reviewed. 1. The owner can supply a source API key and page identity or saved responses; source credentials are read once from the source's fixed origin and never stored. 2. The dry run counts every component, group, incident and its updates, maintenance window and subscriber as imported, changed, skipped or refused, with reasons, and writes no record. 3. Changing either the source or Lamp page after review refuses application and requires a fresh dry run. 4. A dry run names each excess subscriber over a SUB-020 channel capacity and refuses excess rows; an over-limit apply writes nothing until a narrowed review fits.
MOVE-001.now: Move in previews a switch from Statuspage, Better Stack, Instatus or Sorry before writing Lamp records, and applies only the exact source and page state the owner reviewed. **Acceptance.** 1. The owner can supply a source API key and page identity or saved responses; source credentials are read once from the source's fixed origin and never stored. 2. The dry run counts every component, group, incident and its updates, maintenance window, subscriber and exposed notice or update template as imported, changed, skipped or refused, with reasons, and writes no record. For Sorry, the dry run and saved job also account for every supplied field path as mapped, changed, raw-only, deleted or refused, with a reason and next action; unknown nested fields, shortened text and unsupported resource files cannot be silently ignored. 3. Changing either the source or Lamp page after review refuses application and requires a fresh dry run. 4. A dry run names each excess subscriber over a SUB-020 channel capacity and refuses excess rows; an over-limit apply writes nothing until a narrowed review fits.

migrations.buyerSteps: Back up data and owner source before deployment. After updating the checkout and installing frozen dependencies, rer deploy applies this migration after 0081 before starting the updated Worker. It allows reinstated maintenance to be cancelled again while retaining the unique scheduled, reminder, started and completed notices. Existing maintenance and notice history is preserved. Check cancellation, reinstatement and a second cancellation after updating. No new account or credential is required.

Back up data and owner source before updating. Apply this additive migration after 0082 with rer deploy. Existing templates keep their kind and choices. Sorry notice and update templates retain source metadata and private wording; review status, audience and affected services in the composer before publication. No provider account or new credential is required. Run Edit Run fleet, 18 November 2026.

agentUpdateInstructions: From v1.11.22, back up data and owner source, then restore and exercise a copy before adopting the update. Update the checkout to v1.11.23, run pnpm install --frozen-lockfile (the checkout pins @runeditrun/rer 0.2.121), and run rer deploy with the same environment and input file. Apply 0082_repeated_maintenance_cancellation.sql and 0083_sorry_template_metadata.sql in order before starting the updated Worker. Preserve the original deployment checkout, ownership records and Cloudflare account credentials for guarded rer signin to the app Worker. Name a second copy with --environment and leave LAMP_RESOURCE_PREFIX unset. Preserve the intended mail configuration. The default is MAIL_PROVIDER=none. For enabled email, explicitly select the intended provider. For deliberate MAIL_PROVIDER=none, follow the 1.11.19 notes and docs/deploy.md, including removal of conflicting sender, sending credentials, relay settings, DKIM inputs and secondary mail-provider configuration. Keep the backup and check sign-in, first-run, Settings, published incidents, maintenance cancellation and reinstatement, and mail or text delivery where configured. Review imported Sorry templates, audience, affected services and status before publishing. Earlier installations follow the retained release history, including migration 0081 and INSTALLATION_KEY custody. Preserve immutable release records, applied migration history, owner customizations, recorded Worker names and hosting inputs. After successful publication and pointer readback, R2 cleanup keeps the current and previous snapshots. A failed publication deletes nothing. Check the published status page after deployment. Run the existing verifier, release validator and affected owner workflows before adopting. Run Edit Run fleet, 2026-11-18.
